title: Bitemporal memory
point: Record when a fact was true and when the system learned it, append corrections instead of overwriting, and you can replay exactly what the system believed at any moment.
definition: Bitemporal memory stores two times for every fact: valid time, when it was true in the world, and system time, when the system recorded it. Corrections append a new version and mark the old one superseded.

objective.text: Given a history of facts and corrections, answer an as-of query: what the system believed at one system time about one valid time.

misconceptions.claim: Updating the record in place is fine as long as the latest value is correct.
misconceptions.correction: Overwriting destroys what the system believed before. You can no longer explain past answers, audit a decision or replay a learner's history.

misconceptions.claim: One timestamp per fact is enough.
misconceptions.correction: One timestamp cannot separate a late correction from a real change. A move reported five weeks late needs both the date it happened and the date the system learned it.

l1: Valid time says when a fact was true in the world, such as an address from 1 April. System time says when the system recorded it, such as 6 May.
A correction never edits the old record. It appends a new version and stamps the old one with the time it was superseded, so every past belief stays readable.
An as-of query takes two dates: the moment in the world you are asking about and the moment of knowledge you are asking from. It returns what the system believed then about that moment.
l2: A customer moved on 1 April but told the company on 6 May. Before 6 May, the system believed the old address held for April; from 6 May it believes the new one.
An agent shipped a parcel on 20 April to the old address. Querying as of 20 April shows it used the best knowledge available then, which settles the complaint fairly.
A mistyped address recorded on 2 March was superseded on 16 March. Queries as of before 16 March return the error, later queries return the correction, and both records remain.
l3: Bitemporal storage costs space, because corrections add rows rather than replacing them. A user fact that changes four times a year builds about 40 versions in ten years, which is small.
The pay-off is replay. When debugging an agent run, query memory as of the run's start time to see exactly what it read, not today's corrected values.
Deletion on request is the exception to append-only. Erase the personal values themselves, and keep only a tombstone recording that a deletion happened and when.
